s.note: Craig's first night hanging out with Austin
s.how: Slice 2 blocks of haloumi (500g) 1cm thick and pat dry. Warm 4 tbsp honey with 1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tbsp cider vinegar for 2 minutes. Heat a heavy pan over medium-high heat with 1 tbsp oil and sear the haloumi 1 to 2 minutes a side until deep golden. Arrange on a platter, drizzle with the hot honey and a squeeze of lemon, and scatter with torn mint and toasted sesame seeds.

s.n: From-scratch French onion dip and chips
s.note: hanging out back at Austin's place
s.how: Slowly cook 2 thinly sliced onions in 30g butter for 25 minutes until deep golden. Cool and chop. Mix with 300g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayo, half a tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp chopped chives, salt and pepper. Chill 1 hour so the flavours settle. Serve with 200g thick-cut salted potato chips.

m.note: the dinner party Craig plans to win Austin back
m.how: Boil 1kg baby potatoes 15 minutes, smash on an oiled tray and roast at 220C for 30 minutes. Chop a bunch of parsley, 2 garlic cloves and 1 red chilli and mix with 100ml olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar and dried oregano. Season 1kg rump steak and grill on a very hot barbecue 4 minutes a side for medium rare. Rest 8 minutes, slice and spoon the chimichurri over. Serve with the potatoes and a dressed green salad.

w.how: Heat the oven to 120C. Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp white vinegar. Spoon 8 tall cloud shapes onto lined trays and bake 50 minutes, then cool in the turned-off oven. Top with 300ml whipped cream, 150g berries, the pulp of 2 passionfruit and a drizzle of lemon curd.

d.note: trying to keep up with the cool neighbour
d.how: Chill 4 pint glasses in the freezer for 30 minutes. Mix the juice of 1 pink grapefruit with 1 tbsp sugar syrup and 400ml cold soda water. Pour 200ml cold pale ale into each glass, then top with the grapefruit soda. Add a squeeze of lime and a grapefruit wedge. For non-drinkers, use ginger beer in place of the ale.
